'''Vicki Leigh Colvin''' (born October 12, 1965) is a professor of engineering and molecular pharmacology at [[Brown University]], and has been selected as the next dean of the [[Louisiana State University]] College of Engineering. At Brown, she is the director of the Centre for Biomedical Engineering. Her work focuses on the synthesis and characterization of [[nanomaterials]]. She is a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]].

== Early life and education ==
Colvin was inspired to study science after watching her mother drink coffee.<ref name=":0">{{Cite magazine |url=http://discovermagazine.com/2000/oct/featwatch|title=20 Young Scientists to Watch |magazine=Discover |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> She is the daughter of Harry Colvin and Carolyn Collins. She earned her bachelor's degree in chemistry and physics at [[Stanford University]] in 1988.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nny.sites.acs.org/vickicolvinnenm2018.htm|title=Vicki Colvin NENM 2018|website=Northern New York Local Section|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldsciencefestival.com/participants/vicki-colvin/|title=Vicki Colvin|website=World Science Festival|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> She completed her doctoral studies in 1994 under the supervision of [[Paul Alivisatos]] at the [[UC Berkeley College of Chemistry]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/tree.php?pid=82741|title=Chemistry Tree - Vicki L. Colvin Family Tree|website=academictree.org|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pines.berkeley.edu/people/vicki-colvin|title=Vicki Colvin |website=Pines Lab |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> After completing her PhD, Colvin joined [[AT&T Bell Laboratories]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.browndailyherald.com/2014/05/20/vicki-colvin-named-new-provost/|title=Vicki Colvin named new provost|last=Dubin|first=Michael|date=2014-05-20|website=Brown Daily Herald|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> Here she worked on materials for [[holographic data storage]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://nanoparticlelibrary.net/contributor.asp?ID=12|title=Vicki L. Colvin, Rice University |website=Nanoparticle Information Library |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref>

== Career ==
Colvin was appointed to [[Rice University]] in 1996 as part of their expansion in [[nanotechnology]].<ref name=":2" /> She was awarded a [[Phi Beta Kappa]] teaching prize and named as [[Discover (magazine)|Discover magazine]]'s Top Scientists to Watch.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://archive.epa.gov/oswer/nanotechnology/web/html/ia-introduction-biography.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181219044033/https://archive.epa.gov/oswer/nanotechnology/web/html/ia-introduction-biography.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 19, 2018|title=Biography of Dr. Vicki Colvin |website=Nanotechnology for Waste and Cleanup |publisher=US EPA |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> Her research was supported by a fellowship from the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]].<ref name=":3" /> She pioneered the use of water-soluble quantum dots in biomedicine.<ref name=":8">{{Cite journal|date=2006-09-29|title=Water-soluble quantum dots for biomedical applications|journal=Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications|volume=348|issue=3|pages=781–786|doi=10.1016/j.bbrc.2006.07.160|pmid=16904647|issn=0006-291X|last1=Yu|first1=William W.|last2=Chang|first2=Emmanuel|last3=Drezek|first3=Rebekah|last4=Colvin|first4=Vicki L. |bibcode=2006BBRC..348..781Y }}</ref> The quantum dots can be encapsulated into amphiphilic polymers, which allows control of the quantum dot toxicity.<ref name=":8" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chang|first1=Emmanuel|last2=Thekkek|first2=Nadhi|last3=Yu|first3=William W.|last4=Colvin|first4=Vicki L.|last5=Drezek|first5=Rebekah|date=2006|title=Evaluation of Quantum Dot Cytotoxicity Based on Intracellular Uptake|journal=Small|volume=2|issue=12|pages=1412–1417|doi=10.1002/smll.200600218|pmid=17192996|bibcode=2006Small...2.1412C |issn=1613-6829}}</ref> As a model for tissue localization following intradermal infiltration, Colvin studied how quantum dots migrate in mice.<ref name=":9">{{Cite journal|last1=Howard|first1=Paul C.|last2=Walker|first2=Nigel J.|last3=Colvin|first3=Vicki L.|last4=Yu|first4=William W.|last5=Warbritton|first5=Alan R.|last6=Siitonen|first6=Paul H.|last7=Cozart|first7=Christy R.|last8=Webb|first8=Peggy|last9=Roberts|first9=Dean W.|date=2007-07-01|title=Migration of Intradermally Injected Quantum Dots to Sentinel Organs in Mice|journal=Toxicological Sciences|volume=98|issue=1|pages=249–257|doi=10.1093/toxsci/kfm074|pmid=17404394|issn=1096-6080|pmc=3471152}}</ref> She found that 1D quantum dots remain as a deposit on the skin and penetrate the nearby [[subcutis]] and were distributed to draining lymph nodes.<ref name=":9" /> She bound quantum dots to gold nanoparticles with a [[peptide sequence]], which suppresses luminescence; allowing the combination to be used as probes for targeted degradation.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2005-09-09|title=Protease-activated quantum dot probes|journal=Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications|volume=334|issue=4|pages=1317–1321|doi=10.1016/j.bbrc.2005.07.028|pmid=16039606|issn=0006-291X|last1=Chang|first1=Emmanuel|last2=Miller|first2=Jordan S.|last3=Sun|first3=Jiantang|last4=Yu|first4=William W.|last5=Colvin|first5=Vicki L.|last6=Drezek|first6=Rebekah|last7=West|first7=Jennifer L. |bibcode=2005BBRC..334.1317C }}</ref> She investigated how the shape of quantum dots impacted their function and toxicity.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Colvin|first1=Vicki L.|last2=Buhro|first2=William E.|date=March 2003|title=Semiconductor nanocrystals: Shape matters|journal=Nature Materials|volume=2|issue=3|pages=138–139|doi=10.1038/nmat844|issn=1476-4660|pmid=12612665|bibcode=2003NatMa...2..138B|s2cid=13634895}}</ref> She demonstrated that weathering quantum dots in acidic and alkaline conditions can increase the [[Bactericide|bactericidal]] activity due to the rapid release of cadmium and selenite ions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mahendra|first1=Shaily|author-link1=Shaily Mahendra|last2=Zhu|first2=Huiguang|last3=Colvin|first3=Vicki L.|last4=Alvarez|first4=Pedro J.|date=2008-12-15|title=Quantum Dot Weathering Results in Microbial Toxicity|journal=Environmental Science & Technology|volume=42|issue=24|pages=9424–9430|doi=10.1021/es8023385|pmid=19174926|issn=0013-936X|bibcode=2008EnST...42.9424M}}</ref> Her group worked on other nanomaterials, including [[fullerene C60]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2005-12-01|title=Nano-C60 cytotoxicity is due to lipid peroxidation|journal=Biomaterials|volume=26|issue=36|pages=7587–7595|doi=10.1016/j.biomaterials.2005.05.027|pmid=16005959|issn=0142-9612|last1=Sayes|first1=Christie M.|last2=Gobin|first2=Andre M.|last3=Ausman|first3=Kevin D.|last4=Mendez|first4=Joe|last5=West|first5=Jennifer L.|last6=Colvin|first6=Vicki L.}}</ref>

At [[Rice University]], Colvin was appointed the Kenneth S. Pitzer-Schlumberger Professor of Chemistry.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.rice.edu/people/vicki-colvin |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181219044723/https://chemistry.rice.edu/people/vicki-colvin |archive-date=2018-12-19 |title=Vicki L. Colvin |website=Department of Chemistry |publisher=Rice University |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> Her work continued to consider the interactions of nanoparticles, with applications in water purification.<ref name=":4" /> She is particularly interested in how nanoparticles interact with living systems.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://www.slb.com/about/foundation/board/bio_colvin.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181219044149/https://www.slb.com/about/foundation/board/bio_colvin.aspx |archive-date=2018-12-19 |title=Vicki Colvin |website=Schlumberger |access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> She investigated [[cerium oxide]] nanocrystals, and whether when they could be used for medical applications when coated in [[oleic acid]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.rice.edu/2013/10/14/rice-scientists-create-a-super-antioxidant/|title=Rice scientists create a super antioxidant|website=news.rice.edu|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lee|first1=Seung Soo|last2=Song|first2=Wensi|last3=Cho|first3=Minjung|last4=Puppala|first4=Hema L.|last5=Nguyen|first5=Phuc|last6=Zhu|first6=Huiguang|last7=Segatori|first7=Laura|last8=Colvin|first8=Vicki L.|date=2013-11-26|title=Antioxidant Properties of Cerium Oxide Nanocrystals as a Function of Nanocrystal Diameter and Surface Coating|journal=ACS Nano|volume=7|issue=11|pages=9693–9703|doi=10.1021/nn4026806|pmid=24079896|bibcode=2013ACSNa...7.9693L |issn=1936-0851}}</ref> Colvin led a UK-US scientific effort to create a framework to regulate the use of nanomaterials.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.rice.edu/2011/01/27/us-uk-join-forces-for-nano-safety/|title=US, UK join forces for nano safety|website=news.rice.edu|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> She delivered the 2012 [[Arthur M. Sackler]] Colloquium, talking about the properties of nanoparticles.<ref>{{Citation|last=Arthur M. Sackler Colloquia|title=Vicki Colvin-Nanotechnology|date=2 July 2012 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BPDe2RfpbHA|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> In 2013 Colvin was named by [[Chemistry of Materials]] as one of their most highly cited investigators. Her recent research looks at [[sorbent]]s that can help to remove [[arsenic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.susnano.org/SNO2017/pdf/Presentation_SNO_Colvin.pdf|title=Towards Living Nanoscale Sorbents|last=Colvin|first=Vicki|website=Sus-Nano|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref>

=== Academic service ===
Colvin was director of the [[National Science Foundation]] Center for Biological and Environmental Nanotechnology from 2001 to 2011.<ref name=":1" />  She was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2007 and the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]] in 2011.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.coursera.org/instructor/~2280464|title=Professor Vicki Colvin, Instructor|website=Coursera|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aimbe.org/college-of-fellows/cof-1410/|title=Vicki Colvin, Ph.D. COF-1410 - AIMBE|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> She became the vice provost for research at [[Rice University]] in 2011.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chron.com/business/article/People-in-Business-2080481.php|title=People in Business|last=Chronicle|first=Houston|date=2011-07-10|website=Houston Chronicle|access-date=2018-12-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.rice.edu/2011/07/13/colvin-and-farach-carson-named-to-vice-provost-positions/|title=Colvin and Farach-Carson named to vice provost positions|website=news.rice.edu|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> Colvin joined [[Brown University]] as provost in 2014, after a nationwide search, and resigned after less than a year in the position.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite web|url=http://www.browndailyherald.com/2015/05/19/after-only-a-year-colvin-to-step-down-as-provost/|title=Vicki Colvin to step down as Brown University's provost|last=Zappa|first=Joseph|date=2015-05-19|website=Brown Daily Herald|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brownalumnimagazine.com/articles/2014-11-05/keeping-up-with-change|title=Keeping Up With Change|website=www.brownalumnimagazine.com|access-date=2018-12-18}}</ref> She joined the board of the [[Schlumberger Foundation]] that year, with the hope to secure funding for women scientists.<ref name=":5" /> During her time as provost, she created an entrepreneurial education program, reined in the budget deficit and established a vice provost of the arts position.<ref name=":7" /> She stepped down from her role as provost in June 2015 to focus on her research.<ref name=":7" />  She has taught multiple courses for [[Coursera]] and is an advocate for [[flipped classroom]] learning.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":6" /> She is an editor of the journal [[Small (journal)|Small]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2008|title=Starting on Top|journal=Small|volume=4|issue=7|pages=863–866|doi=10.1002/smll.200800822|bibcode=2008Small...4..863. |issn=1613-6829|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Colvin was named the chair of the committee to conduct the quadrennial review of the National Nanotechnology Initiative (NNI) of The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine.<ref>https://www.nationalacademies.org/our-work/quadrennial-review-of-the-national-nanotechnology-initiative-2025#sectionCommittee</ref>
